headline: Mississippi utility Entergy has warned Amazon Web Services that its data centers near Jackson may be cut off from the grid at times of peak demand.
score_reason: Lowered from 6 to 5: the warning dates from earlier this year, The Information first reported it on 8 Oct, and the details rest on two unnamed sources and a thin relay.
importance_line: A big cloud provider may have to run on its own backup generators at busy times so that other electricity customers keep their supply, a sign of how tight the local grid is, but the claim rests on two unnamed sources and the details are thin.
summary: The Information reports, as relayed by Crypto Briefing, that Entergy Mississippi warned Amazon Web Services, Amazon's cloud unit, that it may have to disconnect its Jackson-area data centers from the grid at peak demand to protect supply for other customers, according to two people it cites. Crypto Briefing adds that AWS has since changed its power systems so the sites can switch automatically to backup generators; The Information published the report on 8 Oct and says the warning came earlier this year.
notes: Credit follows the chain to The Information (original reporter). Text read: Crypto Briefing's relay and The Information's public lede only; the full article is behind a subscription wall.
